simple: a small program that watches whether the drone's sensors still agree with each other, and raises an alarm when they stop agreeing.
analogy: Leila noticing that what her eyes say and what her feet feel no longer match.
precise: in this handbook, the learner's module that computes consistency measures of the inputs the navigation trusts (here: compass field strength against its value on the ground, GNSS position against a prediction from GNSS velocity, and GNSS freshness), applies a gate and a persistence time to each, and publishes a latched fault that the vehicle's failsafe logic turns into an action.
source: R1 of MP7 (lab run); C3 of MP7 (pending verification)

simple: how long it takes from the moment something goes wrong to the moment the alarm sounds.
analogy: the steps Leila takes between the floor tilting and her noticing it.
precise: the time between the injection of a fault (known exactly in a simulator) and the first fault published by the monitor; it is at least the persistence time and at most persistence plus the loop period plus any filter delay; a test states its limit before the run, and the report records the margin to that limit.

simple: the same test with your protection switched off, to show that the fault really does harm.
analogy: showing the head waiter that without the new rule, the old accident happens again.
precise: a scenario in a test matrix that injects the same fault with the feature disabled and must reproduce a stated harm (for example "vehicle more than 100 m from home"); without it, a passing test could mean that the injection never reached the vehicle. It plays the role of a negative control in a numerical test.

simple: a problem your feature does not catch, written down on purpose with a test that shows it.
analogy: Leila admitting, in writing, "my rule does not help if the whole room is tilted".
precise: a row of the test matrix that injects a fault outside the feature's claimed coverage, records what happens, and is reported as an open item for the next review gate; it is not counted as a failure, but if its result changes (the gap closes or worsens) the row flags it.

simple: landing straight down without trusting where the drone thinks it is.
analogy: putting the tray down where you stand when you no longer trust your sense of direction.
precise: in this handbook's starter lab, the failsafe action taken on a guard fault: switch to land and zero the horizontal command, so that the vehicle descends without position or heading feedback and drifts with the wind; it trades a bounded drift for not steering on bad data. Real flight stacks have their own degraded modes, which you must look up.
source: R2 of MP7 (lab run); D1, D2 of MP7 (title only, pending verification)

simple: the first real hover, with the drone tied down so that it cannot fly away.
analogy: the first walk with a full tray along a rope handrail.
precise: a hover test in which a tether (or a net enclosure) physically limits where the vehicle can go; it reduces some hazards (flyaway) and adds others (the tether snagging or pulling the vehicle over), so it is planned in the safety case and held only after gate R3.
source: C1 of MP7 (guide 11.6 MP7 card, pending verification)
